title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga County, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga County, PA
metaDescription: Own dry-gas Marcellus minerals near Wellsboro or Tioga County's gas belt? We buy directly, explain deductions honestly, and close without games.
heroLead: Tioga County land has a way of humbling anyone who thinks it's simple. Between the Pine Creek Gorge and the gas belt that runs through the northern townships, no two family tracts here tell quite the same story.
intro: Tioga County sits in the northern tier of Pennsylvania's dry-gas Marcellus window, with Wellsboro as the county seat and a mix of state forest land, working farms, and timber tracts spread across the townships. Shell and Southwestern Energy were among the operators active here during the leasing boom, and while a good chunk of the county's mineral rights sit under land the Commonwealth itself owns through the state forest system, a substantial amount is still held privately by families who've farmed or timbered this ground for generations.

The Marcellus here runs dry, almost pure methane, which means the economics depend heavily on gathering infrastructure and pipeline takeaway capacity rather than natural gas liquids pricing. That infrastructure reality shapes which parts of the county see steady development and which parts have units permitted but sitting quiet, waiting on a pipeline connection that hasn't been built yet.

sections.heading: A County Split Between State Forest and Private Land
paragraphs: Tioga State Forest and Tioga-Hammond Lakes take up a meaningful share of the county's acreage, and mineral rights under state forest land are managed separately through the Bureau of Forestry's own leasing program, not by individual owners. If your family's minerals sit under private land near the forest boundary, though, you're dealing with the same ordinary lease, division order, and royalty questions as anyone else in the Marcellus play, just with development sometimes clustered near the edges of the public land where operators have easier surface access.

That patchwork means unit boundaries in Tioga County can look unusual on a map, weaving around forest tracts and following old farm lot lines instead of neat rectangles. It's worth having someone who actually reads Pennsylvania oil and gas plats confirm exactly which unit your parcel falls in before you agree to any number.

sections.heading: Post-Production Deductions on Northern Tier Leases
paragraphs: Leases signed in Tioga County during the 2008 to 2010 boom carried the same post-production deduction language common across the northern tier, and after Kilmer v. Elexco upheld that language for leases that allow it, owners here have watched gathering, compression, and transportation costs chip away at royalty checks that already reflect a lower wellhead price than wetter counties see. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act protects the one-eighth floor on the gross value, but it doesn't stop deductions from being applied within that calculation if your lease language permits it.

We've sat across the table from Tioga County families who assumed their royalty would track the headline gas price they saw on the news, only to find their actual check running well below that once the deductions were applied. That gap is one of the most common reasons owners decide it's time to sell rather than keep monitoring a statement they don't fully trust.

sections.heading: Act 13 Impact Fees Fund the Townships, Not Your Check
paragraphs: Tioga County and its townships have received Act 13 impact fee revenue since 2012, money that goes toward road repair, emergency services, and other local infrastructure strained by well pad traffic and development. That fee comes from the operator to local government and has nothing to do with your personal royalty. We explain this distinction on every county page because it's one of the most common points of confusion we hear from owners across the northern tier.

sections.heading: Selling Minerals in Tioga County
paragraphs: We start with your deed and any lease or division order paperwork you have, confirm your parcel against current permits and unit filings, and put together a cash offer grounded in what's actually happening on your ground or nearby. If your interest sits near the state forest boundary or in a township with limited pipeline access, we'll tell you honestly how that affects value instead of glossing over it. Closing happens through a title company, with recording handled at the courthouse in Wellsboro.

faqs.question: Do I own minerals under state forest land differently than private land?
faqs.answer: Yes. Minerals under Tioga State Forest are managed by the Commonwealth's Bureau of Forestry, not by private owners. If your interest is under private land near the forest, ordinary lease and royalty rules apply to you directly.

faqs.question: Why does gas development seem uneven across Tioga County townships?
faqs.answer: Pipeline gathering infrastructure varies significantly by township here. Some areas have strong takeaway capacity and steady development, while others have permitted units still waiting on a pipeline connection.

faqs.question: How do post-production deductions affect a dry-gas county like this one?
faqs.answer: Dry gas already sells for less than wet gas per unit, so deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation take a proportionally larger bite out of an already lower wellhead value. Reviewing your lease language is the first step to understanding your specific exposure.

faqs.question: Does the Act 13 impact fee show up on my royalty statement?
faqs.answer: No. It's a separate payment from the operator to county and township government and won't appear anywhere on your division order or royalty check.

faqs.question: What if my mineral interest was never surveyed against the current unit?
faqs.answer: That's common on older Tioga County tracts. We work with title professionals who can confirm exactly how your legal description maps to the current unit before we finalize any offer.
